newsitem.title: FRANCE: Cross-border fund flow seen at $11 trln in 10 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Cross-border fund flow seen at $11 trln in 10 yrs.

text.p: International pension and mutual fund flows from the Group of Seven (G7) countries could reach $11 trillion in the next 10 years, Chris Poll, chairman of fund tracking firm Micropal, said on Thursday.
He told a fund management conference here anticipated higher returns from emerging economies would lead to a larger slice of industrialised countries' investment going abroad.

"In the next 10 years, if 20 percent of all pension and mutual funds invest internationally, $11 trillion will flow across borders out of their domestic country," he said. "Remember what happened when $63 billion left in 1993 (when) most emerging markets doubled."
He said only a small fraction of U.S. and European funds were invested in emerging markets.

The process of increasing international investment in the U.S. would be replicated elsewhere in the developed world, Poll said. Under four percent of French and German mutual funds are currently invested abroad.

"Because of historic conservatism in investment policies, the average German worker needs to contribute around 40 percent more in pension contributions if they are to receive the same as their British counterpart.
"Once the realisation of the facts occurs then, there will be a further significant increase in cross-border flows and investment," Poll said in a paper prepared for the conference.

He said much of the external investment would be through unitised investments which, together with the expansion of retail mutual fund investing, would considerably expand the marketplace and opportunities for the mutual fund industry.
